suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted lacks three essential integration elements that expose Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to material legal risk. Without express merger language declaring this Agreement (together with its incorporated documents) to be the entire agreement between the parties, the counterparty could seek to introduce prior negotiations, side letters, or pre-contractual representations to expand its rights or narrow Sunesis Pharmaceuticals's remedies. The absence of a supersession clause means that earlier agreements on overlapping subject matter could survive in parallel, creating ambiguity about which obligations govern and potentially imposing on Sunesis Pharmaceuticals commitments it did not intend to carry forward. Additionally, without a fraud carve-out, the integration clause could be used to bar Sunesis Pharmaceuticals from pursuing claims arising from fraudulent pre-contractual misrepresentations.
suggestions.original_text: Integration; Precedence. Any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant to this Agreement will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Integration; Precedence. This Agreement, together with any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant to this Agreement (each of which is made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference), constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, supersedes all prior agreements and understandings relating thereto, and does not limit any liability for fraud. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, the clause imposes no active, enforceable duty of care on Quintiles — it merely declares that Sponsor Confidential Information "shall be considered confidential" without specifying the standard to which Quintiles must protect it, leaving Sunesis Pharmaceuticals unable to enforce a minimum protective standard against Quintiles in the event of a disclosure or misuse of its proprietary pharmaceutical data. The clause is also entirely unilateral in structure, addressing only Quintiles as a recipient without imposing explicit, operative obligations on Quintiles to maintain and safeguard that information, which creates an enforcement gap against Quintiles and its personnel. Critically, there is no obligation on Quintiles to return or destroy Sponsor Confidential Information upon termination or expiration of this Agreement or upon Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' written request, meaning Quintiles may retain Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' proprietary data indefinitely after the relationship ends, exposing Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to ongoing competitive and regulatory risk. Counsel should confirm that the survival provision elsewhere in the Agreement covers these confidentiality obligations for a period extending beyond termination.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter "Sponsor Confidential Information") written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor. Quintiles shall protect Sponsor Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than reasonable care. Upon Sponsor's written request or upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Quintiles shall promptly return or destroy all Sponsor Confidential Information in its possession or control.

suggestions.reason: The current Confidential Information identification standard relies solely on affirmative marking or written confirmation within thirty (30) days, meaning sensitive proprietary data, clinical trial results, or regulatory strategies disclosed by Sunesis Pharmaceuticals without a formal "confidential" label—as commonly occurs in fast-moving pharmaceutical development—would fall outside protection entirely, exposing Sunesis to uncompensated misappropriation of its core assets. Additionally, the need-to-know restriction directs each party to provide Confidential Information only to "the other party," yet imposes no obligation to ensure that employees, subcontractors, or advisors who actually receive that information are themselves bound by written confidentiality obligations, leaving Sunesis with no direct contractual protection against downstream disclosure by Quintiles' personnel. Together, these gaps materially undermine the enforceability of the entire confidentiality regime that is intended to protect Sunesis's proprietary pharmaceutical information throughout the engagement.
suggestions.original_text: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked 'confidential', or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure, or that by its nature or the circumstances of its disclosure a reasonable person would recognize as confidential or proprietary. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information on a need-to-know basis, and solely to those of its employees, contractors, subcontractors, and professional advisors who require access for the undertaking of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those set forth herein. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its authorized personnel only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period of ten (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause captures only IP derived from Sponsor-supplied materials, leaving a material gap for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals: inventions or know-how conceived by Quintiles specifically in performing the Services under this Agreement are not expressly assigned to Sunesis and could be claimed by Quintiles as independent IP. The clause also grants Quintiles no defined license to use Sponsor's Property, creating uncertainty as to the permitted scope of use, and imposes no restriction preventing Quintiles from exploiting Sponsor's Property beyond the Services. Third-party IP infringement responsibility is entirely absent and should be addressed in the Agreement's indemnification provision to ensure Sunesis is protected against claims arising from Quintiles's use of third-party intellectual property in performing the Services.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor's Property. Sponsor's property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how (i) related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, or (ii) conceived or developed by Quintiles in performing the Services under this Agreement, and all such inventions, trade secrets and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively "Sponsor's Property"). Quintiles is hereby granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Sponsor's Property solely for the purpose of performing the Services under this Agreement, and Quintiles shall not use Sponsor's Property for any other purpose.

suggestions.reason: The clause defines Quintiles' Property by reference to IP "developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement," but does not expressly confine that definition to background IP — that is, IP developed prior to this Agreement. This creates a material risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals because IP developed by Quintiles during the performance of Services, but not incorporating Sponsor data, could be characterised as "independent of this Agreement" and therefore claimed by Quintiles rather than treated as foreground IP governed by Section 6.3a. Additionally, the avoidance-of-doubt sentence contains a drafting error — "Sponsor's Property of Sponsor Confidential Information" — which, as written, is internally incoherent and could allow Quintiles to contest the scope of the carve-out that is intended to protect Sunesis Pharmaceuticals. Both defects should be corrected to close the foreground IP gap and restore the clarity of the Sponsor-derived IP carve-out.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles’ Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement, which relates to Quintiles’ business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively “Quintiles’ Property”). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles’ Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor’s Property of Sponsor Confidential Information.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles' Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles prior to or independently of this Agreement and the Services performed hereunder, which relates to Quintiles' business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively "Quintiles' Property"). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles' Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how developed in connection with the performance of Services under this Agreement, nor any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor's Property or Sponsor Confidential Information.

suggestions.reason: The clause assigns Project IP to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals but is silent on what happens if that IP, as delivered by Quintiles, infringes a third party's intellectual property rights, leaving Sunesis exposed to infringement claims with no contractual remedy or recourse against Quintiles. Because Quintiles controls the manner in which the Services are performed and the methods used to generate Project IP, any infringement risk originates with Quintiles, yet the current drafting places the entire burden of that risk on Sunesis once the assignment is made. Without a warranty of non-infringement and a corresponding indemnity obligation on Quintiles, Sunesis could receive tainted IP and bear the full cost of defending and resolving third-party claims. This gap is particularly material given that Project IP is also deemed Sponsor Confidential Information under Section 5.1, amplifying the downstream consequences of a defective or encumbered assignment.
suggestions.original_text: Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively “Project IP”) are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively "Project IP") are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Quintiles represents and warrants that, to the best of its knowledge, the Project IP does not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights, and Quintiles shall indemnify and hold harmless Sponsor against any third-party claims arising from any such infringement to the extent caused by Quintiles' performance of the Services. Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.

suggestions.reason: The clause creates three material risks for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals. First, the license to Quintiles Software expressly excludes Sunesis's Affiliates and third-party contractors, which could prevent Sunesis from engaging its own group companies or service providers to access study data it has contracted and paid to generate. Second, the license carries no stated duration, exposing Sunesis to the risk that Quintiles asserts the license lapses upon Agreement expiry even where the Quintiles Software remains the only practical means to retrieve regulatory-critical study data. Third, the clause addresses ownership of Quintiles' Property improvements only where those improvements do not incorporate Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor's Property, but is entirely silent on the ownership of improvements that do incorporate such Sponsor materials, leaving a foreground IP gap that could be exploited against Sunesis.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles’ Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor’s Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs, is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles’ Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles' Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor's Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. Any improvements to Quintiles' Property that incorporate Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor's Property shall be the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs) is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license, with the right to use such software programs by Sponsor and its Affiliates and contractors acting on Sponsor's behalf, without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. Such license shall remain in effect for the duration of this Agreement and for so long thereafter as such Quintiles Software remains necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles' Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted only addresses the negative — prohibiting either party from acquiring rights in the other's intellectual property — but fails to include an affirmative statement that each party retains ownership of its own pre-existing intellectual property. For Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, whose core commercial value lies in its proprietary patents, compound know-how, and drug development data, the absence of an express pre-existing IP retention provision creates a material risk that ownership of background intellectual property could be disputed, particularly where such intellectual property is incorporated into or used in connection with services performed under the Agreement. Without an affirmative vesting sentence, a counterparty could argue that the negative restriction alone is insufficient to establish that Sunesis's pre-existing intellectual property remains its exclusive property throughout and after the term of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: No Implied Rights. Except as expressly provided herein, neither party shall have any right, title or interest to or in any patents, patent applications, know-how (whether patentable or not) or other intellectual property rights of the other party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: No Implied Rights. Each party retains all right, title, and interest in and to its intellectual property owned or developed independently of this Agreement. Except as expressly provided herein, neither party shall have any right, title or interest to or in any patents, patent applications, know-how (whether patentable or not) or other intellectual property rights of the other party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to material compliance risk on three fronts: it contains no anti-bribery or anti-corruption obligation on Quintiles, meaning Sunesis could face regulatory and reputational liability for Quintiles' conduct under applicable anti-corruption laws without any contractual backstop; there is no mutual obligation to notify the other party of a breach of law or policy affecting performance, leaving Sunesis uninformed of issues that could jeopardize its clinical programs or regulatory submissions; and the clause is entirely silent on forced labour, child labour, and human trafficking in Quintiles' supply chain, a standard due-diligence requirement that Sunesis, as a regulated pharmaceutical sponsor, would be expected to have addressed. Additionally, Quintiles' standard operating procedures are referenced but not required to be made available to Sunesis, limiting Sunesis's ability to assess compliance and prepare for regulatory inspections.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA's electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 ("Part 11"), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles' standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order, and Quintiles shall make its relevant standard operating procedures available to Sponsor upon written request. Quintiles shall take commercially reasonable steps to address forced labour, child labour, and human trafficking in its supply chain. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law or regulation that affects the performance of the Services under this Agreement. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted gives Sunesis Pharmaceuticals a unilateral termination-for-convenience right but is entirely silent on what follows termination: there is no obligation on Quintiles to return study data or clinical trial materials, no transition or handover obligation, no requirement to cooperate with a replacement CRO, no exit-period service standard or pricing, and no specification of which provisions survive. For a pharmaceutical company managing ongoing clinical trials, this creates acute operational and financial risk — Quintiles could cease all activity on Day 31 of notice with no obligation to transfer data or assist an incoming provider, leaving Sunesis Pharmaceuticals unable to continue trial operations or satisfy regulatory obligations. The absence of a survival clause also means that confidentiality, payment, and intellectual property obligations are not expressly preserved post-termination, creating enforcement gaps that could directly prejudice Sunesis Pharmaceuticals.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Quintiles. Upon any such termination, Quintiles shall provide reasonable transition assistance, including return of Sponsor's data and documentation in a mutually agreed format and cooperation with any replacement provider designated by Sponsor, for up to ninety (90) days following the effective date of termination at the rates set forth in the applicable Work Order. The obligations of confidentiality, payment for Services rendered through the effective date of termination, and intellectual property assignment shall survive termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The current provision requires only that the parties "promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule" following an uncured breach, with no defined deadline for that meeting, no requirement that Quintiles deliver a formal transition plan, and no obligation to transfer data, work product, or regulatory materials to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals or a successor vendor. Given the nature of Quintiles' clinical research and pharmaceutical services — which may encompass active trials, regulatory submissions, and sensitive study data — the absence of a structured transition obligation exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to significant operational and regulatory disruption if services are terminated. Without an obligation on Quintiles to cooperate with a successor service provider or relinquish materials in an orderly manner, Sunesis Pharmaceuticals could face gaps in clinical operations or loss of continuity with ongoing regulatory work. The provision should be anchored to a defined timeframe and expanded to impose a transition assistance obligation on Quintiles.
suggestions.original_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days' written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall, within ten (10) days following such expiration, meet to prepare a close-out and transition plan addressing the orderly transfer of data, work product, and regulatory materials to Sunesis, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations and shall provide reasonable transition assistance to Sunesis or any designated successor service provider during such transition.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the termination clause imposes no obligation on Quintiles to assist Sunesis Pharmaceuticals in transitioning ongoing Projects to a successor vendor or in-house team following termination; Quintiles need only cease work and submit a final accounting. For Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, whose pharmaceutical development activities depend on continuity of clinical and regulatory data, work product, and operational handover, this gap creates material operational and regulatory risk: a sudden cessation without structured transition could disrupt active studies, delay regulatory submissions, and leave Sunesis without the data or records needed to continue work. The absence of a transition assistance obligation should be remedied by inserting a targeted, enforceable duty on Quintiles to provide reasonable transition support upon Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' request.
suggestions.original_text: Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, shall provide such reasonable transition assistance as Sunesis Pharmaceuticals may request to transfer the affected Project(s), including all associated data, materials, and work product, to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals or its designee, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting.

suggestions.reason: The clause permits Quintiles to delegate performance to any affiliate without Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' prior consent and, critically, does not expressly preserve Quintiles' primary liability for that affiliate's performance — meaning if an affiliate fails to perform, Sunesis Pharmaceuticals may be forced to pursue the affiliate directly rather than holding Quintiles accountable under the Agreement. This creates material financial and operational risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals across all Work Orders. Additionally, the residual limb of the "control" definition — "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" — contains a typographical error ("polices") and sets no objective threshold, rendering the scope of "affiliate" impermissibly vague and potentially sweeping in entities with mere informal influence as parties entitled to exercise all of Quintiles' contractual rights against Sunesis Pharmaceuticals. The overbroad and unenforceable control definition could expose Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to obligations toward, and claims by, unvetted entities well beyond those Sunesis Pharmaceuticals would reasonably have agreed to extend rights to under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order; provided that Quintiles shall remain primarily liable for the performance of any such affiliate as if Quintiles had performed such obligations directly. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor's affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor's affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term "affiliate" shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term "control" shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity, or otherwise having the ability to direct the policies and operations of an entity through ownership, contract, or otherwise.

suggestions.reason: The clause creates a material gap in Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' oversight rights by carving out Quintiles' corporate affiliates entirely from the prior written approval requirement, while a companion provision in the same Agreement confirms that affiliates may freely perform any of Quintiles' obligations with only a blanket pre-agreement from Sponsor. This directly conflicts with the approval mechanism designed to protect Sunesis, because Quintiles can circumvent Sponsor consent entirely by routing work through affiliated entities—potentially of any size, capability, or regulatory standing—without affording Sunesis any meaningful evaluation right. Additionally, condition (i) requires that Quintiles provide "sufficient information to enable proper evaluation," but neither the standard for sufficiency nor any review period for Sunesis is defined, leaving Quintiles free to characterise minimal disclosure as adequate and depriving Sunesis of an objective benchmark for exercising or denying approval.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0,6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (including to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract or the use of such corporate affiliate, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor or affiliate, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor or affiliate on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0, 6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors or affiliates; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract or affiliate agreement.

suggestions.reason: The third sentence of this clause operates entirely in Quintiles's favour: it shields Quintiles from liability for any errors, delays, or consequences attributable to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals's cooperation failures, while imposing no equivalent protection on Sunesis if Quintiles fails to cooperate or supply necessary information. This one-sided structure creates material financial and operational exposure for Sunesis, which could be left without any contractual remedy for Quintiles-caused delays that Quintiles attributes broadly to a "cooperation" shortfall. The undefined phrase "or to otherwise cooperate" compounds the risk by enabling Quintiles to invoke the exclusion on the basis of imprecise, unspecified obligations that no court could objectively assess without recourse to extrinsic evidence. Additionally, Sunesis's own delivery obligation is anchored only to the vague standard "in a timely manner," which provides no objective trigger or deadline and could be weaponised against Sunesis when disputes arise over whether a document or item was supplied with sufficient speed.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles promptly following Quintiles's written request all documents, materials and information in Sponsor's possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Neither party shall be liable to the other nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising solely and directly from the other party's failure to timely provide documents, materials or information expressly required under the relevant Work Order or Change Order, provided that the party seeking to invoke this provision has first provided the other party with written notice of the specific deficiency and the other party has failed to remedy such deficiency within ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such notice.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to two compounding risks. First, the word "immediately" imposes a notification standard that is practically unachievable and subjectively assessed, meaning Quintiles could argue that any delay in Sunesis's written notice—however brief—constitutes a breach, potentially shifting liability for downstream schedule or cost impacts onto Sunesis. Second, "good faith efforts" is an undefined and legally indeterminate standard: without an objective benchmark, Quintiles retains broad discretion to characterize Sunesis's negotiating conduct as deficient and use that characterization to resist resolution or assert breach, particularly where disputes over Work Order delays escalate into broader claims under the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing promptly upon becoming aware of any material delays or limits encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause imposes on Sunesis Pharmaceuticals an unlimited and unconditional assumption of risk of loss for all shipments, with no carve-out where Quintiles's own negligence or willful misconduct caused or contributed to the loss — including scenarios where Quintiles selects, instructs, and contracts with the carrier on Sunesis's behalf. The blanket disclaimer of liability for third-party carriers compounds this exposure by shielding Quintiles even where it negligently selected or inadequately instructed the carrier, leaving Sunesis with no recourse for losses attributable to Quintiles's conduct. In the pharmaceutical context, where shipped materials may include high-value clinical supplies or regulatory documents, this uncapped and fault-blind risk allocation creates material financial exposure for Sunesis with no corresponding protection.
suggestions.original_text: If Sponsor delivers, ships, or mails materials or documents to Quintiles, or requests that Quintiles deliver, ship, or mail materials or documents to Sponsor or to third parties, then the expense and risk of loss for such deliveries, shipments, or mailings shall be borne by Sponsor. Quintiles disclaims any liability for the actions or omissions of third-party delivery services or carriers.
suggestions.suggested_fix: If Sponsor delivers, ships, or mails materials or documents to Quintiles, or requests that Quintiles deliver, ship, or mail materials or documents to Sponsor or to third parties, then the expense and risk of loss for such deliveries, shipments, or mailings shall be borne by Sponsor, except to the extent arising from Quintiles's negligence or willful misconduct. Quintiles disclaims any liability for the actions or omissions of third-party delivery services or carriers, except where such loss arises from Quintiles's negligent selection of such carrier.

suggestions.reason: The Work Order states only that it "relates to" the Master Agreement, which is insufficiently precise to establish that the Master Agreement governs and controls the services to be performed under this Work Order. For Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, this creates a material risk that Quintiles could argue the Master Agreement's protections — including indemnification, liability caps, and IP ownership provisions — do not apply to this specific engagement, leaving Sunesis exposed without its negotiated contractual safeguards. Additionally, the clause fails to identify any attachments or exhibits to the Work Order as constituent documents, meaning scope, specifications, or pricing schedules appended to this Work Order may be disputed as non-binding. This gap interacts critically with any order-of-precedence provision in the Master Agreement that depends on the Work Order being clearly identified as a subordinate, governed document.
suggestions.original_text: This Work Order (“Work Order”) is between ________ (“Sponsor”) and ________ (“Quintiles”) and relates to the Master Services Agreement dated ________, (the “Master Agreement”), which is incorporated by reference herein. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: This Work Order ("Work Order") is between ________ ("Sponsor") and ________ ("Quintiles") and is subject to and governed by the Master Services Agreement dated ________ (the "Master Agreement"), which is incorporated by reference herein, together with all attachments and exhibits to this Work Order. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.

suggestions.reason: The current clause acknowledges that this Work Order is "subject to" the Master Agreement but fails to establish an explicit order of priority in the event of a conflict between the two documents, leaving Sunesis Pharmaceuticals exposed to arguments that a later-issued Work Order implicitly supersedes or modifies the protections Sunesis negotiated in the Master Agreement. Without an express conflict-resolution hierarchy, a counterparty could contend that specific Work Order terms prevail over the Master Agreement, potentially displacing key Sunesis protections such as liability limitations, indemnification provisions, or IP ownership rights. The clause also contains no exclusion of extraneous terms, creating a risk that the counterparty's standard terms, online terms, or purchase order conditions could be incorporated by reference or by conduct.
suggestions.original_text: Work Order. This document constitutes a “Work Order” under the Master Agreement and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Work Order. This document constitutes a "Work Order" under the Master Agreement and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement, which shall prevail in the event of any conflict between the two documents. No other terms or conditions shall apply.

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no operative payment terms whatsoever, deferring entirely to attachments that themselves are not reproduced in the reviewed text, leaving Sunesis Pharmaceuticals with no enforceable baseline governing how fees are calculated, when invoices are issued, when payment falls due, how fee changes are controlled, or how disputed amounts are treated. This creates material financial exposure for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals: without an agreed payment timeline, invoice dispute mechanism, or late-payment consequence, the counterparty could issue invoices on an ad hoc basis, demand immediate payment, and characterize any withholding by Sunesis Pharmaceuticals as a breach. The absence of an expense pre-approval requirement further risks Sunesis Pharmaceuticals being presented with unreasonable cost claims it has no contractual basis to reject. At minimum, the clause must include a compact set of operative payment mechanics to give Sunesis Pharmaceuticals enforceable rights independent of attachment content.
suggestions.original_text: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6
suggestions.suggested_fix: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6. Fees shall be as set forth in Attachment 2 and shall not be increased without prior written agreement of Sunesis Pharmaceuticals. Invoices shall be issued in accordance with Attachment 4 and are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Sunesis Pharmaceuticals may dispute any invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, and undisputed amounts shall remain due and payable. Late payments on undisputed amounts shall accrue interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower. Out-of-pocket expenses are reimbursable only to the extent pre-approved in writing by Sunesis Pharmaceuticals and set forth in Attachment 2.

suggestions.reason: The Term clause exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to significant operational and financial risk because it does not require Attachment 1 to specify the scope, deliverables, timeline, or fees, leaving the precise obligations of the counterparty undefined and potentially unenforceable. The clause also lacks any change control mechanism, meaning the counterparty could assert scope changes without Sunesis Pharmaceuticals's written consent, creating uncontrolled cost and schedule exposure. The conflict-resolution relationship between this Work Order and the Master Agreement is only partially addressed, with no express statement that the Master Agreement governs in the event of inconsistency, which creates interpretive uncertainty that could disadvantage Sunesis Pharmaceuticals in a dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Term. The term of this Work Order, the scope of services, deliverables, timeline, fees, and pricing basis for which shall be set forth in Attachment 1, shall commence on the date of execution by authorized representatives of both parties and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement. Any modification to this Work Order requires a written amendment signed by authorized representatives of both parties. This Work Order is subject to the Master Agreement, which shall govern and control in the event of any conflict. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

suggestions.reason: While the clause requires Quintiles' corporate affiliates to be bound by all terms of the Master Agreement and this Work Order, it imposes no equivalent obligation on third-party subcontractors and consultants, who are merely listed without any contractual commitment to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' protections. This creates a material gap for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals: sensitive proprietary data, confidential information, and clinical research materials handled by those subcontractors would not be subject to the confidentiality, data security, or data protection standards agreed under the Master Agreement, leaving Sunesis Pharmaceuticals exposed to unauthorized disclosure or misuse with no direct contractual recourse against the subcontractor. Given that Quintiles remains responsible for performance of the Services, Quintiles should be required to flow down at minimum the equivalent obligations to any subcontractor or consultant it engages. The confidentiality and data protection provisions of the Master Agreement should be verified to confirm they survive expiry or termination and would extend to cover any breach by a subcontractor through Quintiles' primary liability.
suggestions.original_text: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles’ affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below:
suggestions.suggested_fix: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles' affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below. Prior to engaging any such subcontractor or consultant, Quintiles shall bind each such subcontractor or consultant in writing to obligations no less protective of Sunesis Pharmaceuticals than those imposed on Quintiles under the Master Agreement and this Work Order, including without limitation obligations relating to confidentiality, data protection, and data security. Quintiles shall remain primarily liable to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors and consultants to the same extent as if Quintiles had performed such Services directly.

suggestions.reason: The subcontractor placeholder as drafted imposes no requirement that Sunesis Pharmaceuticals provide prior written approval before Quintiles engages any third-party subcontractor or consultant, leaving Sunesis exposed to unknown parties performing sensitive pharmaceutical services without its knowledge or consent. Critically, the clause contains no provision holding Quintiles liable for the acts or omissions of those subcontractors, meaning that if a subcontractor causes a regulatory failure, data breach, or study error, Quintiles could disclaim responsibility and Sunesis would be left without a contractual remedy against the party it contracted with. This gap is particularly material given the regulated clinical research context, where subcontractor performance directly affects Sunesis's regulatory submissions and patient safety obligations.
suggestions.original_text: [Insert names of any subcontractors or consultants, other than Quintiles’ affiliates, that will be used]
suggestions.suggested_fix: [Insert names of any subcontractors or consultants, other than Quintiles' affiliates, pre-approved in writing by Sponsor prior to engagement]. Quintiles shall remain responsible for the acts and omissions of all such subcontractors and consultants to the same extent as if Quintiles had performed such Services directly.
